## A K-8 School for Girls
#### Hamlin is a vibrant and inclusive community that expects and encourages diversity of thought, experience, and beliefs.
As a culminating class project, Grade 8 students collaborate creatively on a scripted or devised performing arts production to perform for the Hamlin community in June before their graduation. This musical production offers students an opportunity to develop and share their skills in music, dance, acting, technology, and visual design (with set, props, costumes, and lighting) while bonding together as a class. Students work on their performing arts project over the course of the spring semester. These annual Grade 8 musical productions are based on meaningful content aligned with Hamlin’s mission and Creed and have been a favorite school tradition.
Intentionally placed in the middle of our 2-year U.S. history curriculum, Grade 7 students spend a week in Washington D.C. to explore our nation's capital, learn more about our federal government, and connect with the city and each other. Highlights include visits to important sites such as the U.S. Capitol Building, national museums, and the National Mall, as well as an alumni panel of Hamlin graduates who now live and work in Washington DC.
In our Grade 6 _Rise to the Challenge_ capstone project, students work in small teams to explore different ways in which Hamlin students can identify and meet the challenges of their time at school. Teams create a proposal letter about their selected challenge, and collaborate on a creative component for a capstone group presentation (film, podcast, theatrical performance, etc.). Goals of this project include practicing teamwork and project management, thinking deeply about the Hamlin experience, celebrating what works well and providing constructive feedback on making our school better, expressing ideas through creative and meaningful formats, and building confidence in public speaking and presenting.
> Our Grade 5 Entrepreneurship Capstone Project immerses students in the world of small business and product creation as they ideate, build, and manage their very own small businesses from start to finish. Students gain an understanding of what it takes to create a business and the role female entrepreneurs play worldwide. As part of this project, students work in small teams to submit a business proposal, develop a product, gain hands-on experience in marketing, budgeting, customer research, and cost/profit modeling, and apply for a "micro-loan" to help fund their startup materials. At the end of the year, students "sell" their products at our Capstone Market!

## A K-8 School for Girls
#### Hamlin is a vibrant and inclusive community that expects and encourages diversity of thought, experience, and beliefs.
The Jan Micha Influential Women in History Program is a way for Grade 4 students to learn about women who have made significant, positive, and often overlooked contributions that have changed the course of American herstory. Research, public speaking skills, and learning about different experiences through influential women’s stories are core principles of this project. Originally called the Famous American Women Program, it was renamed in 2015 to honor one of the program’s founders and beloved member of Hamlin’s faculty for over 30 years, Jan Micha.
Our Grade 3 students embark on an immersive, year-long journey through the diverse landscape and history of the Golden State. This interdisciplinary capstone project centers on "stories from the land and the people," moving beyond traditional dates to explore the often untold narratives of California’s Indigenous People and the lived experiences of immigrants. Through a blend of student-centered research, collaborative small-group work, expository writing, and excursions to historically significant state landmarks like Angel Island, students sharpen their mapping skills and utilize modern technology to analyze how geography and resources have shaped human movement over time.
In this vibrant interdisciplinary capstone project, Grade 2 students dive deep into the heart of San Francisco to explore what it truly means to be a member of a community. Through the lens of our beautiful “City by the Bay," students work in small groups to research the rich history, cuisine, activities, and community resources of neighborhoods beyond their own, sparking a lifelong curiosity for local exploration and beyond. This journey takes them far beyond the classroom as they navigate public transit to visit landmarks, secure their first library cards, and tour City Hall to lay the foundation for future civic studies in Sacramento (Grade 4) and D.C. (Grade 7). The adventure culminates in a creative fusion of geography and engineering: students master cardinal directions by mapping neighborhoods and collaborate with our Maker teacher to 3D-print iconic SF landmarks. Whether through a custom travel brochure, digital video, or other final product that changes from year to year, our students emerge with a profound sense of place and a collection of materials and learning that showcases their growth as urban explorers and engaged citizens.

## A K-8 School for Girls
#### Hamlin is a vibrant and inclusive community that expects and encourages diversity of thought, experience, and beliefs.
In Grade 1, students begin the year by exploring identity. They learn about themselves, their families, and what makes each person unique. This foundational work helps students build a strong sense of self and develop empathy for others.
Building on this understanding, students then engage in a project-based study of their community and neighborhood. They begin by observing their surroundings and generating their own questions about the people, places, and living things around them. From these explorations, students develop topics based on their interests, such as caring for the environment, supporting people in need, or making their community more inclusive.
Guided by questions like _What does our community need? Who or what needs our help? How can we make a difference?_ students investigate their ideas through real world experiences. They go out into the neighborhood, interview community members and local experts, and work in small groups to deepen their understanding.
The study culminates in meaningful action. Students design and carry out projects that contribute to their community in authentic ways, such as creating awareness campaigns, organizing donation drives, building solutions, or sharing their learning with others. Through this process, students see themselves as capable, compassionate community members who can make a real impact.
Every spring, our Kindergarten classes begin their Emergent Units. The themes of these units are completely student centered, different between the classes, and vary every year. Themes are based on class discussions around interests and curiosities. Once the theme is determined, homeroom teachers get to work connecting with outside specialists and our in-house specialist teachers to integrate local and diverse activities and guest experts to heighten the learning experience. The culminating project is then shared with the larger community through performances, public speaking, and interactive, hands-on opportunities.

At Alverno, we steadfastly place our confidence in God’s providence to build community by fostering love, respecting individual dignity, nurturing kindness and friendship, while instilling hope to seek a way to make a difference with perseverance. The Catholic tradition of faith, service and academic excellence is evident on the campus where students embrace God’s love as they develop self-confidence and lasting school pride. Mission Statement of Alverno Heights Academy  
Alverno Heights Academy is an independent, Catholic school for girls and boys in grades TK-8. The school is dedicated to preparing our students to function in a society as informed, knowledgeable persons, who have the requisite skills to make and implement mature decisions about complex problems. Enlivened by the spirit of the Immaculate Heart Community tradition, and mindful of the Franciscan roots of its founders, Alverno’s program– academic, spiritual, aesthetic, social, and physical– is shaped by the staff, trustees, and students considering the world for which the students are being educated. Alverno Heights Academy intends to prepare knowledgeable individuals of conscience and conviction to function in their world with the courage to take risks in the pursuit of values, and with the ability to apply untried solutions to problems. We also intend to create an environment in which students can develop the humility and humor needed to learn from their mistakes; in which they can experience the joy that comes from behaving with a spirit of generosity; and in which they can grow in the compassion necessary to live as peacemakers in the global community.

## What _parents_ say
"Our daughter has been with Hello, Mandarin! for a number of years — starting in nursery and growing through the program with joy. The approach is playful and immersive, rooted in music, storytelling, and cultural activities. It is particularly wonderful for young learners with no prior Mandarin background. This spring, she received an offer from The Brearley School. We are so grateful."

## What _parents_ say
#### — **Brearley School**
“Our daughters (now 17 and 14) have been learning Mandarin with Dr. Lyu since they were in preschool, continuing with virtual lessons when we couldn't meet in person. Her approach to immersive language is extremely affective and our daughters have grasped the language through music, conversation, and dance. Their progress has exceeded our expectations, and when they speak, people often think we have a native Chinese speaker in our family who has taught them. We love the program and are so happy that we found it.”

## What _parents_ say
#### — Horace Mann School
"Our two children have been taking Mandarin with Dr. Lyu since age 2 — both from a non-Chinese-speaking home. We are amazed to say that what emerged from her joyful, music-and-arts-based approach is two children who speak Mandarin with the confidence of native speakers. Our daughter received an offer from The Brearley School in Spring 2024, and our son received an offer from The Buckley School in Spring 2026. Hello, Mandarin! does not just teach language. It builds it from the inside out."

## What _parents_ say
#### — **Buckley School**
"It has been such a joy — three years with Hello, Mandarin!, and our daughter has grown in ways that go far beyond language. This spring, she received an offer from The Spence School. We are so grateful for Dr. Lyu and everything this program has given our family."

## What _parents_ say
#### — **Spence School**
Dr. Lyu is an exceptionally talented musician and an equally gifted educator - she is patient, kind, and adaptable, but establishes challenging goals for her students. Our two young children have been taking piano with her for about 8 years, since they were 3 and 4 years old. They adore Jiao Jiao and their weekly piano class (even remote classes during Covid). I couldn’t be more pleased with what they have learned and the opportunities offered along the way.

## What _parents_ say
#### — Trinity School
"Our son attends Hunter College High School, where Mandarin is a rigorous subject with frequent quizzes, tests, and examinations. He was struggling to keep up. Dr. Lyu took the time to understand exactly what Hunter required, tailored his curriculum to the school's vocabulary and exam format, and built Hunter's confidence from the ground up. He now studies twice a week with Hello, Mandarin! His grades at Hunter have improved significantly — but more importantly, he walks into every Mandarin class ready, instead of dreading it. That change is everything."

## Everything you’d like to _know._
Every child is placed in the right cohort for their level, not just their age. Contact us and we'll find the perfect fit.
*   Six is the maximum that allows our method to work.
Mandarin is a tonal language — every child needs to hear their own voice, be corrected in real time, and participate in every single moment of class. In a group of six, nothing slips through. Every child is seen, heard, and challenged at their level.
It is also why our results speak for themselves.
*   Hello, Mandarin is the only UES program where the full examination pathway — YCT, HSK, and AP Chinese — is built into the curriculum from day one, not added as a separate tutoring service. Every cohort, from 籽 Seeds through 华 Brilliance, is designed around this arc. The result is a documented, verified record of Mandarin proficiency that strengthens any independent school or college application. 

*   Most Hello, Mandarin families don't — and our program is intentionally designed for non-Mandarin-speaking households.
Children receive rich, immersive input in every class through songs, stories, movement, and daily routines. We also provide simple at-home supports — short audio demos, Quizlet sets, and Joyreader levels — that any parent can use in two minutes a day, with no Mandarin background required.
Your child can thrive here. We make the learning joyful, structured, and achievable for every family.
*   Yes. Mandarin proficiency is an increasingly valued asset in New York City independent school admissions, and we are proud that our students have been admitted to The Brearley School, The Spence School, Horace Mann, Buckley, Nightingale-Bamford, Avenues, and more.
We support families by ensuring their child's Mandarin journey is documented and verifiable — from Lincoln Center performances to YCT and HSK examinations — so that proficiency becomes a concrete, demonstrable strength on any application.
We are happy to discuss your child's timeline and goals, and to help build their unique profile for success. Reach out at [info@hellomandarin.org](mailto:info@hellomandarin.org).   
*     
Many parents remember weekend classes focused on memorizing characters and copying worksheets. Hello, Mandarin! takes a joyful, play-based approach that nonetheless achieves ambitious learning outcomes. Our curriculum is:

## Everything you’d like to _know._
*   Research-driven and aligned with NYC independent school early childhood practices

    *   Play- and story-based, using songs, picture books, movement, and hands-on activities

    *   Highly immersive, with bilingual bridges that ensure understanding without breaking the language environment

    *   Purposefully small-group, giving every child authentic speaking opportunities every single class

    *   Developmentally aligned, meeting each child where they are — from 18 months through high school
Instead of rote memorization, children acquire Mandarin naturally — by listening, responding, singing, acting, reading stories, and performing on stage at Lincoln Center.
*
Hello, Mandarin! offers unlimited make-ups within the same semester. To keep our small-group classes safe, high-quality, and joyful for every child, here is how it works:
*   Make-ups must be scheduled before the semester ends

    *   Make-ups are offered based on space availability

    *   Please schedule by email at least 24 hours in advance — no drop-ins

    *   For classes offered once per week, we will do our best to find a suitable alternative time or group at the right age and proficiency level
Just email us at [info@hellomandarin.org](mailto:info@hellomandarin.org) and we will find the best spot for your child.
*   Hello, Mandarin! welcomes new families on a rolling basis throughout the year. Our program runs three terms — Fall (September–December), Spring (January–June), and Summer (中文游 Summer Atelier) — and new students may join whenever a spot becomes available.
We work with children from age 18 months through 12th grade, and many of our families have been with us since the very beginning of that journey. Current families and siblings of enrolled students receive priority enrollment each term.
To inquire about current availability, please reach out at [info@hellomandarin.org](mailto:info@hellomandarin.org) or complete the form on our Admissions page. We respond as soon as possible.
*   Yes — and our students' records speak to that directly.

**St Mary's School**, Cambridge, England, is a private school run in the Catholic tradition, offering day and boarding provision for girls aged three to eighteen. The school occupies three sites within walking distance of each other, and Cambridge city centre, close to the University Botanic Gardens, with sports facilities a short distance away on Long Road and a Boathouse for rowing on the River Cam.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge
## History
[edit]
St Mary's School, Cambridge, was founded 1898 by the Sisters of Mary Ward and the Institute of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who had also founded a [school of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mary's_School,_Ascot "St Mary's School, Ascot") in Ascot, Berkshire 13 years earlier. The sisters started out with two day girls and two day boarders. In 1904 the swelling numbers necessitated a change of venue and 'The Elms' on Bateman Street was purchased for £6,000. The house had a tradition that was very much in keeping with Mary Ward's vision. It had previously belonged to Benjamin Hall Kennedy, former Regius Professor of Greek at Cambridge University. As the school continued to grow, other premises were added. Paston House was purchased in 1909.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mary's_School,_Cambridge#cite_note-1)
The Junior School was part of St Mary's School, Cambridge, until it closed in 1987, when it reopened as St Catherine's Prep School and was governed by a group of parents who became the board of directors. In 2007 St Catherine's became St Mary's School, Cambridge's junior section. Both schools are governed by a single board.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge
## Boarding
[edit]
The school offers a full, weekly or flexi boarding programme for years 5 to upper sixth (ages 9 to 18).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mary's_School,_Cambridge#cite_note-2) Approximately 20% of senior school pupils board.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mary's_School,_Cambridge#cite_note-3) In 2016 the school purchased a new dedicated boarding house on Brooklands Avenue, Mary Ward House, to replace the two buildings previously used: Bateman House for sixth formers and 'The Elms' for girls from years 7–11.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mary's_School,_Cambridge#cite_note-4)

# St Mary's School, Cambridge
## History
[edit]
St Mary's School, Cambridge, was founded 1898 by the Sisters of Mary Ward and the Institute of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who had also founded a [school of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mary's_School,_Ascot "St Mary's School, Ascot") in Ascot, Berkshire 13 years earlier. The sisters started out with two day girls and two day boarders. In 1904 the swelling numbers necessitated a change of venue and 'The Elms' on Bateman Street was purchased for £6,000. The house had a tradition that was very much in keeping with Mary Ward's vision. It had previously belonged to Benjamin Hall Kennedy, former Regius Professor of Greek at Cambridge University. As the school continued to grow, other premises were added. Paston House was purchased in 1909.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Mary's_School,_Cambridge#cite_note-1)
The Junior School was part of St Mary's School, Cambridge, until it closed in 1987, when it reopened as St Catherine's Prep School and was governed by a group of parents who became the board of directors. In 2007 St Catherine's became St Mary's School, Cambridge's junior section. Both schools are governed by a single board.

The history of all-girls boarding schools in the United States dates back to the 19th century, when educators began to recognize that girls should have access to the same high-quality academic education as boys. As society progressed, these schools became essential institutions for nurturing female leadership, independence, and intellectual confidence.
Today, within the U.S. boarding high school system, several exceptional all-girls schools honor tradition while embracing innovation. They offer girls safe, focused, and supportive learning environments, making them an increasingly popular choice for many Chinese families in recent years.

## Here are some advantages of all-girls schools:
1. **Focused Learning Environment**: All-girls schools often provide a learning atmosphere tailored specifically for girls, allowing them to thrive academically without the distractions that can occur in co-ed settings.

2. **Empowerment and Confidence**: These schools emphasize leadership and self-expression, helping students build confidence and develop strong personal identities.

3. **Strong Female Role Models**: All-girls schools typically employ female teachers and administrators, offering students positive role models who can inspire and mentor them.

4. **Encouragement of Participation**: Girls may feel more encouraged to participate in sports, sciences, and other traditionally male-dominated fields, fostering a sense of equality and ambition.

5. **Reduced Social Pressures**: With the absence of boys, students may experience fewer social pressures related to dating and appearance, allowing for a greater focus on personal growth and academics.

6. **Collaborative Environment**: These schools often promote teamwork and collaboration, encouraging students to work together and support one another in their pursuits.

7. **Tailored Curriculums**: The curriculum can be designed specifically to meet the interests and needs of girls, often resulting in enhanced engagement and academic success.

8. **Community and Friendship**: Students often develop strong bonds with their peers, creating a supportive community that can last a lifetime.

9. **Focus on Personal Development**: All-girls schools typically place a strong emphasis on character development and social responsibility, preparing students to be compassionate leaders in society.
**_These advantages contribute to the unique benefits of an all-girls educational experience._**
Below, we recommend several outstanding U.S. all-girls boarding schools, hoping to help more families find the ideal environment for girls to thrive.

## Schools and locations
**1. Miss Hall's School, Massachusetts**
Miss Hall's School was founded in 1898 and is one of New England's most distinguished historic private girls' schools. Located in Pittsfield, Berkshire County, Massachusetts, the 90-acre hillside campus offers beautiful surroundings and access to rich academic resources from nearby top universities.
Ranked among the top five girls' schools in the U.S. with an A+ overall rating, Miss Hall's offers nearly 100 courses, including its signature Hallmark advanced curriculum, as well as three levels of ESL programs. The school is especially known for its acclaimed Horizons experiential program and girls' leadership initiatives, which emphasize holistic development and social responsibility. With exceptional college counseling—led by a former Williams College admissions officer—100% of graduates matriculate to well-known universities, and many international students are admitted to U.S. Top 50 institutions.
**2. Woodlands Academy of the Sacred Heart, Illinois**
Founded in 1858, Woodlands Academy of the Sacred Heart is a highly respected Catholic independent girls' school that blends rich tradition with innovative education. Located in the safe and quiet town of Lake Forest, it is near Chicago and just a 30-minute drive from Northwestern University.
Ranked the #1 girls' school in Illinois and recognized as a National Blue Ribbon School, Woodlands offers a rigorous college-preparatory curriculum along with specialized programs in STEM, computer science, and global studies. The school also excels in visual arts, music, and performing arts, with graduates regularly accepted into top art institutions. Woodlands maintains a 100% college placement rate, with students attending Northwestern, the University of Chicago, Brown University, Johns Hopkins University, and other elite universities.
**3. Saint Mary's School, North Carolina**
Saint Mary's School is a top private, all-girls boarding school located in Raleigh, North Carolina's capital city. With an A+ rating, the school is recognized for its exceptional academics and ranks within the top 12% of U.S. private high schools. Its faculty is highly experienced, with an average of 16 years of teaching experience, and more than 80% holding master's or doctoral degrees.
